- When sentiment shows strong bullish (≥0.67) or bearish (≤-0.33) momentum in recent days, model tends to overreact — adjust forecast downward if sentiment is bullish, upward if bearish, especially in early horizon.
- Model consistently overestimates early spikes (e.g., 80s → 82s) and underestimates late spikes (e.g., 85s+), suggesting lag in capturing momentum shifts — apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting for late-period corrections.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 81.91 → 84.62) — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak if sentiment is strong, or reduce by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d mean, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation; if below, add 2–5% unless sentiment is bearish.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts often overestimate; 20+ day forecasts underperform — adjust for horizon decay: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per additional day beyond 15.
